- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots in next period; apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.0% to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (e.g., first 3–5 days of forecast) — especially when sentiment is volatile — so apply slight upward bias for first 3–5 days if sentiment is bullish.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3–5 day moving average of past 10–15 days as baseline for correction.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >2% for 2+ consecutive days, apply downward adjustment of 0.5–1.0% per day to prevent runaway overestimation.
- For long-term horizon (e.g., 30d), model often overestimates near end of forecast — especially if sentiment is positive — reduce final 3–5 days by 0.5–1.5% to reflect diminishing momentum.
